name: Vidyarthi Bhavan
blurb: Legendary benne masala dosa, served since the 1940s.
story: Started in 1943 as a students' mess near Gandhi Bazaar, it is the textbook example of a Bengaluru heritage eatery: tiny menu, cast-iron tawas, a line out the door and a loyalty that crosses generations.
tip: Go on a weekday before 9 am; weekends can mean a long wait. Order the masala dosa and filter coffee.

name: Mavalli Tiffin Rooms (MTR)
blurb: Rava idli and a full Karnataka meal since 1924.
story: MTR is widely credited with popularising rava idli - improvised during a rice shortage in the 1940s, as the story goes. The old dining room still carries the feel of a Bengaluru that ate carefully and slowly.
tip: The famous meal is a ritual: seat yourself, settle in, and finish with the complimentary badam drink if it's served.

name: CTR (Shri Sagar)
blurb: Crisp, butter-laden benne masala dosa in a tiny old-school hall.
story: A Malleshwaram institution from the early 20th century, known for its butter dosa and for tables where strangers share elbow-room and opinions.
tip: Expect shared tables and cash-friendly speed. Pair with a kaapi.

name: Brahmin's Coffee Bar
blurb: A tiny standing-room counter famous for idli-vada and strong filter coffee.
story: A neighbourhood legend whose menu is short and whose queue is long. The idli arrives with chutney and a tangy kudumu-style sambar that regulars defend fiercely.
tip: It's cash-and-hurry style and usually closes by early afternoon - go in the morning.

name: VV Puram Food Street (Thindi Beedi)
blurb: A whole lane of dosas, holige, chaats and sweet shops after dark.
story: The street comes alive every evening with vendors, regional snacks and rotating specialities; during festivals it is among the best-loved eating lanes in the old city.
tip: Do a slow lane walk first, then pick two or three stalls - portions are generous.

name: Veena Stores
blurb: Soft idlis, vada and kesari bath, served fast and hot.
story: Another old Malleshwaram favourite that rewards early risers. Its popularity is quiet and constant, built on consistency.
tip: Arrive before 8:30 am. Combine it with a Malleshwaram market walk.

name: Koshy's
blurb: A long-running cafe where writers, journalists and lawyers have argued for decades.
story: Opened in the 1940s, Koshy's is the city's best-known old-world cafe - dark wood, slow fans and conversations that last longer than the coffee.
tip: Come between meals when it's quieter; try the classic English-style breakfast.

name: Shivajinagar Ramzan Nights
blurb: Grills, haleem, kebabs and sweets in a seasonal night-time food street.
story: During Ramzan the lanes around Russell Market and Mosque Road turn into one of the city's great seasonal food events - an all-night celebration of kebabs, haleem and phirni.
tip: Go with an empty stomach and a group - and plan transit in advance; roads fill up.

name: Meghana Foods
blurb: The Andhra-style boneless biryani that built a citywide cult.
story: A modern Bengaluru institution that grew from a single outlet into a city-wide brand; the biryani and Andhra meals draw late-night and lunch-hour crowds in equal measure.
tip: There are many outlets; pick a less-central one for a shorter wait.

name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
blurb: 240 acres of botanical history with a Victorian glasshouse and an ancient rock.
story: Begun under Hyder Ali in the 18th century and expanded by Tipu Sultan and later the British, Lalbagh holds one of the country's oldest botanical collections. Its glasshouse draws Republic Day and Independence Day flower shows. The Kempegowda watchtower on the rock marks the old city's boundary.
tip: Morning walkers' club hours (early) are the best; the Republic Day flower show gets very crowded - book ahead.

name: Cubbon Park
blurb: A shaded green spine through the old Cantonment-era administrative core.
story: Laid out in the 1870s and named after a former Commissioner, Cubbon Park is dotted with statues, a Greek-style library, a bandstand and the red-brick High Court buildings. It's where retirees, runners and chess players share the same footpaths.
tip: Weekday mornings are best. Some roads are vehicle-free on specific days; check current rules.

name: Bangalore Palace
blurb: A Tudor-revival palace inspired by Windsor Castle.
story: Built in the late 19th century for the Wodeyars, its turrets and carved wood make it one of the city's most photographed landmarks. Large concerts and cultural events are often hosted on its grounds.
tip: Audio guide is worth it; check the event calendar for any closures.

name: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace
blurb: A teak and pillared summer retreat from the late 1700s.
story: Finished in 1791 and modelled on Tipu's Daria Daulat in Srirangapatna, the palace combines Indo-Islamic arches with ornate painted woodwork. It's a short walk from the Fort and Venkataramana temple.
tip: Combine with Kote Venkataramana Temple and KR Market on a single old-city walk.

name: Dodda Basavanna Gudi (Bull Temple)
blurb: A monolithic granite Nandi from the Kempegowda era and the heart of the groundnut fair.
story: Built in the 16th century, the huge Nandi is linked to a local folk story about a bull that was grazing in a groundnut field. That story is the origin of the annual Kadalekai Parishe, the groundnut fair held on the nearby streets.
tip: Visit in the morning; during the fair, expect crowds and detours.

name: Gavi Gangadhareshwara Temple
blurb: A rock-cut cave temple famed for a Sankranti sun phenomenon.
story: Dedicated to Shiva and dated to the Kempegowda era, the cave temple is known for the evening when the setting sun's rays are said to pass through a gap and illuminate the deity - a draw every Makar Sankranti.
tip: Arrive well before sunset on Sankranti; temple custom and timing apply.

name: Vidhana Soudha
blurb: The neo-Dravidian seat of the state legislature.
story: Completed in the mid-1950s under Chief Minister Kengal Hanumanthaiah, it fuses granite and Dravidian styles. It's illuminated on certain days and public holidays.
tip: Interior entry needs permission; photograph the façade from Cubbon Park side.

name: St. Mary's Basilica
blurb: A Gothic-style basilica with a major September feast.
story: One of the oldest churches in the city, its feast in early September attracts people of every faith. The surrounding market turns into a fair.
tip: Avoid driving during the feast week; use the metro.

name: Halasuru Someshwara Temple
blurb: A Vijayanagara-style temple with a lovely gopura near Ulsoor Lake.
story: Dating to the Vijayanagara period, it has some of the city's finest carved pillars and a colourful gateway. It sits within a few minutes of Ulsoor Lake.
tip: Combine with a walk around Ulsoor Lake.

name: Visvesvaraya Industrial & Technological Museum
blurb: Hands-on science for families, next to Cubbon Park.
story: Named for engineer-statesman Sir M. Visvesvaraya, the museum is one of the city's best family rainy-day options, with working exhibits and a dinosaur gallery.
tip: Closed on some public holidays; verify timings.

name: Ranga Shankara
blurb: The city's theatre home, founded by Arundhati Nag.
story: Opened in 2004, Ranga Shankara shows plays in Kannada, English, Hindi and more through the year. Its annual theatre festival is among the country's most celebrated.
tip: Book online - popular shows sell out. The cafe is a gem.

name: Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath
blurb: A fine-arts institution known for its January art street fair.
story: Chitra Santhe, held on Kumara Krupa Road, brings thousands of artists from across India to sell directly to visitors. The Parishath's galleries also hold year-round exhibitions.
tip: On Santhe day come early, carry cash/UPI and expect heavy crowds.

name: Chowdiah Memorial Hall
blurb: A concert hall shaped like a seven-string violin.
story: Built in memory of the violinist T. Chowdiah, the hall's violin-shaped structure is one of the city's most distinctive buildings. It hosts Carnatic and Hindustani concerts, plays and dances.
tip: Check shows on BookMyShow or the venue page.

name: National Gallery of Modern Art
blurb: Modern and contemporary art in a restored heritage mansion.
story: Housed in a heritage mansion, the gallery lets you see a century of Indian modern art in a quiet environment.
tip: Check opening days before visiting.

name: KR Market (City Market)
blurb: Asia-scale flower and vegetable chaos - the city's oldest market.
story: The market's flower section is the engine of festival decorations, wedding garlands and temple offerings. Wholesale begins before dawn - it is a lesson in how the city eats and celebrates.
tip: Go at dawn, wear closed shoes, watch your pockets, and take photos with permission.

name: Russell Market
blurb: A colonial-era market with fruit, meat and a neighbourhood vibe.
story: Dating from the early 20th century, Russell Market is among the city's best for fresh meat, fish and fruit. The nearby streets are popular for biryani and chaat.
tip: Wear comfortable shoes and go before lunch.

name: Gandhi Bazaar
blurb: A dense lane of flowers, sweets, books and legendary coffee spots.
story: Gandhi Bazaar is where the old Basavanagudi comes alive - flowers, fruit, silks and some of the best traditional eateries.
tip: Park away and walk - the lane is narrow and crowded.

name: Commercial Street
blurb: The Cantonment-era shopping street for clothes, fabric and jewellery.
story: Commercial Street has been Bengaluru's busiest shopping artery for generations. Bargaining is expected in many stalls.
tip: Compare prices across a few shops before buying.

name: Chickpet & Avenue Road
blurb: Silk sarees, bullion, wholesale and second-hand books in the old pete.
story: The Chickpet-Avenue Road corridor is a time capsule of the old pete trading city, where fabric merchants and booksellers still operate from century-old shops.
tip: Ask the shop for a bill and compare weave quality - silk purity varies.

name: Ulsoor (Halasuru) Lake
blurb: A central lake with boating and a walking loop.
story: One of the city's older tanks, Ulsoor is surrounded by a busy neighbourhood and a Vijayanagara-era temple. The loop is a favourite for runners and photographers.
tip: Avoid weekend afternoons if you want quiet.

name: Sankey Tank
blurb: A tree-lined tank in a busy neighbourhood - a place to slow down.
story: Built in the 1880s to supply the city, Sankey Tank today is a popular walking spot with a pathway, shaded trees and heritage-flavoured surroundings.
tip: Combine with a Malleshwaram breakfast.

name: Hebbal Lake
blurb: A north-Bengaluru lake with waterbirds and a walking trail.
story: Hebbal Lake is a pocket of nature next to one of the busiest flyovers in the city and has waterbirds, boardwalks and a nature trail.
tip: Binoculars help - early morning is best.

name: Jakkur Lake
blurb: A rejuvenated lake that shows what treated wastewater and citizen action can do.
story: Jakkur has been a prominent example of a community-supported lake restoration, with wetlands and birdlife. It's popular with birdwatchers.
tip: Bring a hat and binoculars; weekend mornings can be busy.

name: Bellandur Lake
best: As a study - not a stroll
blurb: Bengaluru's biggest lake and the poster child of urban pollution.
story: Bellandur's foaming surface became national news. It is also the focus of citizen activism and restoration plans. Understanding it means understanding the city's wastewater and urban growth.
tip: Worth reading about before visiting; viewing points are limited.

name: Puttenahalli Lake (JP Nagar)
blurb: A lake restored through community effort in the south.
story: Puttenahalli was rejuvenated through the efforts of local volunteers, and has a bird-friendly shoreline and a walking path.
tip: Combine with Ranga Shankara for a culture + nature day.

name: Church Street & Brigade Road
blurb: A pedestrian-friendly strip of pubs, cafes and bookstores in the centre.
story: Church Street has been a hangout for decades, helped by being so central and walkable. It's a good starting point for first-time visitors.
tip: Weekend nights are very busy; take the metro to MG Road.

name: Indiranagar (12th Main & 100 Feet Road)
blurb: Breweries, restaurants and a dense bar scene in a leafy neighbourhood.
story: Indiranagar is known for its mix of craft breweries, music venues, cafes and fine-dining. It's a favourite for after-work crowds.
tip: Parking is difficult - use the metro or cabs.

name: Koramangala 5th Block
blurb: A lively mix of cafes, pubs and late-night food spots.
story: Koramangala's 5th block is the social hub of the startup crowd - from brunch cafes to bars to comfort food at midnight.
tip: Check closing times - Bengaluru's licensed venues generally close around 1 am; rules can change.

name: Koramangala startup cluster
blurb: Often called the heart of the city's startup scene.
story: From early food-delivery and e-commerce startups to many new-age companies, Koramangala's cafes, coworking spaces and informal founder meetups made it the startup neighbourhood.
tip: Look for community-run meetups, hackathons and open-house days rather than relying only on big conferences.

name: HSR Layout startup cluster
blurb: A younger startup neighbourhood with coworking spaces and food streets.
story: HSR Layout has grown into a major startup base with many small teams, coworking spaces and cafes. Its 27th Main is known for food.
tip: Weekday evenings have the most meetups.

name: IISc & Research Park
blurb: A century-old science institute that anchors the deep-tech ecosystem.
story: Founded in 1909, IISc's campus is leafy and open. Its research spinouts feed the deep-tech startup scene around it.
tip: Check public lectures; campus access rules apply.

name: NSRCEL, IIM Bangalore
blurb: IIMB's entrepreneurship hub, with incubation and mentoring.
story: NSRCEL has supported hundreds of early-stage ventures through incubation and mentoring, and runs programmes for founders at different stages.
tip: Check the current programme calendar before applying.

name: Whitefield & ITPL
blurb: A large east-Bengaluru technology corridor.
story: Whitefield is home to big tech parks and growing residential communities. The metro's eastern extension has changed commute patterns.
tip: Plan around peak traffic.

name: Manyata Tech Park (north)
blurb: One of the city's largest campuses, with global tech firms.
story: A major employment cluster in north Bengaluru. Nearby lakes and food streets help workers unwind.
tip: Lunch spots in Nagavara are well-known to locals.

name: Electronic City
blurb: The original tech-park hub in the south with hardware and IT firms.
story: One of India's oldest tech clusters, it still hosts big names in IT and electronics and a growing startup ecosystem.
tip: The elevated expressway helps; peak-hour traffic still bites.
